problem: The complete canonical scratch read currently allocates an owned String for every A/B row, though comparison, digest update and bounded examples only need that row until the next cursor advance.
implementation: row_text borrows the current Text ValueRef and validates UTF8 with the exact rusqlite0.40.1 Utf8Error(0,error) mapping. Non-text retains InvalidColumnType(0,actual column name,original SQL type). get_ref(0) preserves invalid-index errors; no unsafe UTF8 or lifetime extension.

next_row preserves Rows::next step followed immediately by conversion; next_pair calls A to completion before stepping B. The two independent mutable Rows borrows bound the two returned str references.

The production loop consumes both references for the original equality, examples and independent digests before either cursor advances. The only loop changes replace its two next_row statements with next_pair and remove now-unnecessary as_deref calls.

Both complete A and B spools, all fifteen tables, sorted duplicate ordinal preservation, full EOF, signed-zero Value fallback, independent hashes, all capacity/byte/count limits, full SQLite error paths and the original nine per-table public fields remain unchanged. reviewed_rules: String FromSql uses ValueRef.as_str then ToString.
as_str accepts Text only and reports invalid UTF8 through FromSqlError::Utf8Error; it does not coerce SQL NULL/Integer/Real/Blob.
Row::get maps Utf8Error to rusqlite::Error::Utf8Error(index,error), and InvalidType to InvalidColumnType(index,column_name,data_type). It does not map this UTF8 path to a generic conversion failure.
Row::get_ref narrows the lifetime to the row borrow, valid only until that cursor's next SQLite step; two statements own independent Rows.
